localChanges: Once you know every advance, research carries on into Future Technology 1, 2, 3 and so on, each costing more than the last, instead of piling up with nothing to research (closes #128).
Future Technology can't be traded in a meeting, stolen by a Diplomat or taken with a captured city, and huts never give one.
The Science report names the advance being researched properly, "The Republic" rather than "TheRepublic".

log: `advancesLacked` (in both the negotiation steps and the resolved proposals) leaves out advances marked `repeatable` (core-science), so Future Technology is never offered, taken or handed over in a meeting (civ-clone/web-renderer#128).

The advance outcome needs a non-repeatable advance to be available, as in v474.05, where a Future Technology's prerequisites are never met. With nothing left to discover, the hut gives something else (civ-clone/web-renderer#128).
chore: rebuild registerRules.js.map from its source

`FutureTechnology` is a repeatable advance (core-science), registered with the others. Its requirement is every non-repeatable advance in the game's advance registry, so `requirements` now takes the registry. Each one completed counts towards the cost of the next, as `DiscoveredTechnologyCount` does in v474.05. Capturing a city never takes one (civ-clone/web-renderer#128).
`stealableAdvances` leaves out advances marked `repeatable` (core-science), so Future Technology can't be stolen (civ-clone/web-renderer#128).

An `Advance` with `static repeatable = true` stays in `available()` once it's known, and completing or adding it again appends another instance to `complete()`, so the number held is the count of its instances. Nothing new is saved. Packages that hand advances between players are expected to leave repeatable ones out (civ-clone/web-renderer#128).
